episodes.158673: An upper-level low moved across east-central Florida from the Atlantic and increased instability. Scattered to numerous storms developed over or just inland from the Atlantic coast and moved west while intensifying. A few of the storms produced strong winds gusts along the coast.
episodes.158682: A mid-level disturbance moving north along the periphery of a upper level area of high pressure in a very warm, unstable airmass led to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon and evening hours of July 13th. Two thunderstorms brought isolated wind damage to St. Lawrence county in the form of downed branches and trees.
episodes.158705: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a weak frontal boundary that was nearly stationary across southwest, to east central Minnesota, and over adjacent west central Wisconsin.  Modest instability and enough wind shear allowed for a couple robust storms to develop along this front. One developed near Redwood Falls and dropped quarter size hail in southern Renville County, north of Franklin. Similar thunderstorm cores  that produced quarter size hail near Franklin moved southward into eastern Redwood County but no reports of hail were received. A similar storm developed in the northern suburbs of the Twin Cities and produced quarter size hail.
episodes.158715: Daytime heating led to scattered thunderstorms in the afternoon.
episodes.158717: A midlevel shortwave trough trekked across the Northern Rockies beneath a weakening ridge. This feature tapped into the already present monsoonal moisture to produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. The stronger storms produced gusty winds in excess of 60 mph across portions of west-central Colorado.
episodes.158739: Widespread severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening within an environment of moderate CAPE and moderate shear. A shortwave moved across the Ohio Valley giving support for multiple rounds of convection, primarily in the form of multicell clusters and linear segments. Although damaging winds were the main impact, a few storms also created large hail.  Flash flooding was reported from slow moving thunderstorms in Lycoming and Tioga Counties.
episodes.158790: Afternoon showers and thunderstorms persisted across the region in a typical summer time weather pattern. Abundant moisture lead to locally heavy rain and some storms were strong with gusty winds being the primary hazard.
episodes.158791: Afternoon showers and thunderstorms persisted across the region in a typical summer time weather pattern. Abundant moisture lead to locally heavy rain and some storms were strong with gusty winds being the primary hazard.
episodes.158856: A very persistent weather pattern continued as a strong area of high pressure stayed centered over Nevada on July 12, 2021. Some drier air rounded this high pressure and filtered into New Mexico, but well above normal atmospheric moisture values continued which led to another day of widespread showers and thunderstorms. These thunderstorms were generally sub-severe with no reports of flash flooding received. However, one thunderstorm near Stanley produced one inch hail while another thunderstorm produced a 63 mph wind gust near Sandia Airpark.
episodes.158857: An area of high pressure that had been centered over Nevada for several days finally began to weaken on July 13, 2021, while abundant moisture continued across New Mexico. As this high pressure weakened, a weak embedded disturbance crossed the area. With sufficient moisture, instability, and additional lift from this weak disturbance, another active monsoon day was in store for northern and central New Mexico. The Luna burn scar experienced its most significant flash flooding event of the season so far with slow thunderstorm motions and very heavy rainfall altering the landscape, destroying bridges, and making several roads impassable. Meanwhile, a brief landspout tornado was reported near Madrid, but no damage occurred.
episodes.159004: A midlevel shortwave trough trekked across the Northern Rockies beneath a weakening ridge. This feature tapped into the already present monsoonal moisture to produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding across portions of Grand County in east-central Utah.
episodes.159007: Scattered thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage across northern Maryland, eastern West Virginia and northwestern Virginia.
episodes.159011: A few thunderstorms produced gusty winds over the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.159012: A few thunderstorms produced sporadic damaging wind gusts over western Maryland.
episodes.159104: Potential existed for isolated showers and storms across east-central Nevada and severe winds were produced from a few storms that formed.
episodes.159377: Strong wind gusts associated with afternoon convection reported over Pinellas coastal waters.
episodes.159474: A nearby upper level disturbance promoted a stretch of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia. Around sunset on July 12th, a thunderstorm strengthened to strong levels in Mason County with downburst winds resulting in two downed trees in the county. Pea sized hail was also observed as the storm progressed northward before dissipating.
episodes.159703: A dominant east coast sea breeze regime focused evening convection across inland southeast Georgia. Instability aloft was enhanced by an upper level low over Florida.
episodes.159972: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 12th.  One storm moved very slowly over eastern La Salle and western Grundy Counties.  Torrential rain produced flash flooding in these areas with numerous roads flooded and at least four bridges damaged.
episodes.160062: Storms developed ahead of a cold front across northeastern Minnesota and pushed into northwestern Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of the 13th. While most of the storms remained below severe limits, a few did produce isolated tree damage and quarter-sized hail.
episodes.160232: An upper level low pressure area with very cold temperatures aloft moved towards South FL today through the day. This along with strong daytime heating and high atmospheric moisture led to rounds of strong to severe showers and thunderstorms areawide. Strong wind gusts, flooding, and hazardous marine conditions were the main impacts across the South FL local waters.
episodes.160233: An upper level low pressure area with very cold temperatures aloft moved towards South FL today through the day. This along with strong daytime heating and high atmospheric moisture led to rounds of strong to severe showers and thunderstorms areawide. Strong wind gusts and hazardous marine conditions were the main impact across the South FL local waters.
episodes.160236: A tropical wave over central Cuba interacted with a low pressure in the upper levels to increase atmospheric instability and lead to rounds of strong showers and thunderstorms.  Strong wind gusts and hazardous marine conditions were the main impact across the South FL Atlantic waters.
episodes.160237: A tropical wave over central Cuba interacted with a low pressure in the upper levels to increase atmospheric instability and lead to rounds of strong showers and thunderstorms.  Strong wind gusts and hazardous marine conditions were the main impact across the South FL Gulf waters.
episodes.160265: Northeast Ohio was in the warm sector during the early afternoon through early evening of the 13th as a surface low drifted eastward across central Lake Michigan. The trailing cold front dissipated while also moving eastward. A squall line moved northeastward across northeastern Ohio and produced damaging wind gusts in Trumbull County. These storms encountered moderate instability and DCAPE, and marginally-moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.160266: Northwest Pennsylvania was in the warm sector during the early afternoon through early evening of the 13th as a surface low drifted eastward across central Lake Michigan. The trailing cold front dissipated while also moving eastward. A squall line moved northeastward across northwest Pennsylvania and produced several instances of straight-line wind damage. These storms encountered moderate instability and DCAPE, and marginally-moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.160267: Lake Erie remained in the warm sector as a surface low moved from central Lake Michigan to near northern Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through early evening of the 13th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front moved eastward and dissipated, allowing the residual surface trough axis to near the western end of Lake Erie by early evening. Multiple squall lines moved eastward over and near Lake Erie, and produced gale-force peak wind gusts at several locations along the Ohio shore. These storms encountered moderate instability and DCAPE, and marginally-moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.160540: Two waves of severe storms entered the Ohio River Valley on July 13th. The first, was in the early morning hours. Despite the lack of day time heating, instability was available due to warm, moist advection under southwest flow. Vertical wind shear was also available as a trough approached an area of high pressure and a created a pressure gradient.||During the afternoon, warm and unstable conditions prevailed; dew points stayed in the lower 70s.  Mean-layer CAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg was able to develop.  Due to a gradient between upper high pressure off the east coast and a shortwave trough moving northeast through the Ohio Valley, moderate mid-level flow characterized by 30-40 knots of 0-6km shear prevailed.  This allowed storms to organize into multicellular storm clusters and short line segments.  Many wind damage reports were received, mainly to trees and power lines, although a few reports of structural damage were also noted.
episodes.160582: On July 8th, a cold front dropped south through central Kentucky in a saturated environment. Even with moderate instability and shear values, there was a report of severe wind damage. In the following days, the front stalled and remained in the area causing scattered wind damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.160746: Warm and moist tropical air was present over Central New York when a quasi-stationary warm front slowly moved through the region. These conditions provided supported for severe thunderstorms with damaging winds resulting in numerous reports of trees and wires knocked down. A wind gust of nearly 70 kts was also measured by a mesonet station.
episodes.160811: A quasi-stationary upper level trough centered across the central Mississippi valley remained in place as a large omega block upstream across the western conus, and a Bermuda upper level ridge worked together to keep the large scale flow pattern rather stagnant.  Heavy rainfall occurred across the Florida panhandle and resulted in areas of flooding.
episodes.160876: A deep moist southwest flow prevailed over the region on July 13th with a bulging Bermuda High to the east and an upper level trough digging in from the Great Lakes region. Air temps in the mid to upper 80s and low 90s created an unstable environment to trigger a few severe thunderstorms that produced damaging winds.
episodes.160880: More than 30 people had to be rescued from Lake Dillon following a microburst, which produced wind gusts as strong as 55 mph.   Paddlers were completely overwhelmed by the sudden and strong wind gusts which flipped them off their boards and kayaks.   Fortunately, Colorado Parks and Wildlife along with the Summit County Sheriff���s Office were already on the water for recovery training.  They quickly picked up stranded boaters from the water and nearby islands, and towed beached boats back to the docks.  No injuries were reported.
episodes.160961: A closed low moved over the Northern Rockies and provided relatively steep mid-levels lapse rates (7C/km+) while a dry sub-cloud layer maintained DCAPE values above 1000 j/kg. An area of relatively weak thunderstorms developed just west of the Townsend area and sent an outflow boundary moving toward the city. Local topography likely played a role in boosting wind gusts to severe levels.
episodes.161019: Scattered thunderstorms produced instances of flooding in northeastern Maryland.
episodes.161171: Monsoonal moisture filtered into Southern California July 11-14, producing thunderstorm activity on July 13 and 14. Moderate rainfall occurred in the San Bernardino County Mountains on July 13 and thunderstorms were reported across the Inland Empire through the mid-morning hours on July 14.
episodes.161227: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.161257: A frontal boundary, coupled with an extremely warm and humid environment, produced another day of slow moving, torrential downpour producing thunderstorms over Central New York. Approximately, 1 to 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time. The Southern Tier was again hit with major impacts from flash flooding of local creeks, streams and overwhelmed storm drainage systems.
episodes.161258: A frontal boundary, coupled with an extremely warm and humid environment, produced another day of slow moving, torrential downpour producing thunderstorms over Northeast Pennsylvania. Stripes of 1 to 3 inch rainfall occurred over several parts of the area. The greatest rain totals occurred over a large part of Bradford county where 3 to 5 inches accumulated in just a few ours. The region was again hit with major impacts from flash flooding of local creeks, streams and overwhelmed storm drainage systems.
episodes.161288: One inch or larger hail fell in Ashton.
episodes.161388: Monsoon moisture slowly seeped into the region under the big dome of high pressure which was causing record-breaking temperatures, fueling isolated to scattered thunderstorms. As the moisture increased, the main thunderstorm impact transitioned from high winds to flash flooding.
episodes.161389: Monsoon moisture slowly seeped into the region under the big dome of high pressure which was causing record-breaking temperatures, fueling isolated to scattered thunderstorms. As the moisture increased, the main thunderstorm impact transitioned from high winds to flash flooding.
episodes.161455: An upper level ridge centered near southern Nevada promoted northeasterly steering flow favorable for bringing storms off the high terrain and into the lower deserts. During the evening on the 12th, strong to severe thunderstorms pushed toward the southwest across southern Gila County where a peak gust of 72 mph was recorded. An outflow boundary from decaying thunderstorms over the high terrain pushed into parts of the lower deserts, allowing a severe thunderstorm to develop over northeastern Maricopa County. This severe thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts across northern parts of the Valley that took down several trees, one of which fell onto a car. No injuries were reported.
episodes.161537: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over Upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.161581: Thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across Pinal, Pima and Santa Cruz counties during the evening hours. One storm produced a funnel cloud near Mt. Wrightston while other storms produced damaging winds and flash flooding in the Tucson Metro area.
episodes.161582: Isolated thunderstorms developed and moved west across southeast Arizona. One storm produced a severe wind gust in southeast Pima County.
episodes.161682: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the late morning and early afternoon July 13th. One isolated damaging wind report was received.
episodes.161703: Scattered gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with thunderstorms enhanced by the presence of a tropical upper tropospheric trough over south Florida and the Florida Keys and strong subtropical high pressure over the western Atlantic.
episodes.161749: A slight risk for severe thunderstorms was outlooked for all of our area with very unstable conditions to the south of a warm front and ahead of a shortwave impulse lifting out of Ohio. CAPE values were running 1500-2000 J/kg, and shear values were running 20-25 knots in the west to 30-40 knots in the east. Wind damage and tropical downpours ended up the main hazards as wet bulb zero heights were over 14,000 feet. Severe thunderstorms were observed across much of the area and the adjoining Great Lakes waters.

episodes.161873: An upper level ridge moved across the northern high plains with mid level northwest flow ahead of it. Moderate instability across much of western Kansas but with weak large scale ascent values with a leeside trough sparking a number of storms out of eastern Colorado. Coupled with moderate shear around 30-35 kts and relatively steep lapse rates, isolated storms pushed across western counties near the Colorado border.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced torrential rain and flash flooding across portions of eastern La Salle County including in Seneca.  Vegetation was flattened near many creeks and channels due to the fast moving flood waters.  Along Hog Run, vegetation was flattened near North 21st Road with debris near the road.  Along North 2350th Road near Armstrong Run, flood waters flowed over the roadway with debris in the channel.  North La Salle Road was flooded, just south of Dupont Road with debris piled on the side of the road along with erosion in the channel.  There was substantial deposition of sediment from a nearby sand and gravel facility across Dupont Road near Deadly Run.  A substantial stretch of Dupont Road was flooded with extensive mud marking on pavement, east of Route 170 near a marina.  Just west of Route 170, the east abutment to the River Road bridge over a small creek was washed out.  A local highway department staff member was driving over this area when the washout occurred.  His truck became stuck on remaining pavement on either side of the washout.  The driver needed to be rescued and refused medical treatment.  Scouring occurred on both sides of the creek with vegetation collapsed or partially collapsed.  Homes on Timmons Lane were flooded with one home suffering a basement wall collapse.  Further west near River Road and Lake Street, flooding of several houses occurred as Spring Brook Creek overflowed with water flowing over fields and into the houses.  Significant damage occurred to vegetation where Spring Brook Creek crossed River Road.  Rainfall of 4.24 inches was reported during a 3 hour period, one mile east of Seneca.  The damage amount was estimated in consultation with local emergency management officials.
Water was reported over a bridge on Highway 181 north of 81.
Route 220 was flooded and possibly washed away.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced torrential rain and flash flooding across portions of western Grundy County.  Vegetation was flattened near many creeks and channels due to the fast moving flood waters.  Along Armstrong Run, water went over the Indian Trail Road bridge.  Damage occurred to the bridge approaches and pavement was missing.  A nearby shed was destroyed and a utility pole was toppled.  Further northeast, the Kinsman Road bridge over Armstrong Run was also damaged.  Significant damage occurred to vegetation including entire trees removed.  Damage also occurred to the Dupont Road bridge over Armstrong Run where the approaches suffered significant scouring.  Vegetation was flattened and a nearby fence was knocked over with evidence of 1 to 2 feet of flowing water.  The Dupont Road bridge over Hog Run was damaged with the approaches washed out.  Vegetation was flattened in many locations near Hog Run between Omalley and Grand Ridge Roads.  Water rescues were performed during the peak of the flooding near Kinsman and Dupont Roads where at least three vehicles were stuck in flood waters.  Rainfall of 6.19 inches was reported during a 3 hour period, four miles northwest of Verona.  Rainfall of 4.58 inches was reported during a 4 hour period, three miles east of Seneca.  The damage amount was estimated in consultation with local emergency management officials.
